mintCompleteness.soleMintSiteVerification: grep 'new KeyPresenceProofRequirement' over src/Precept returns exactly one instantiation (Actions.cs:176). No ProofEngine synthesis site exists for KeyPresence (unlike Presence at ProofEngine.cs:374 or CountContainment at :641). AppendBy is the only action carrying it.
mintCompleteness.logByVsQueueByAsymmetry: ActionKind.EnqueueBy (queue of T by P, Actions.cs:242-251) declares NO ProofRequirements, so a queue-by ordering key mints no uniqueness obligation. This is a real asymmetry, not a mint gap: collection-types.md:384 declares P UNIQUE for 'log of T by P' (audit ordering key), while a queue-by 'by P' is a priority/ordering key that may repeat. KeyPresence(RequireAbsence:true) therefore has exactly one mint occasion family: append-by onto a log-by field.
mintCompleteness.requireAbsencePolarity: RequireAbsence:true -> the key must be ABSENT (uniqueness). Diagnostic on failure is PRE0101 (DiagnosticCode.KeyUniquenessGuard, id 101), selected at src/Precept/Pipeline/ProofEngine.Diagnostics.cs:181-186 by keyReq.RequireAbsence. (RequireAbsence:false would route to PRE0099 KeyPresenceSafety, but no catalog site declares the present-required polarity, so it does not arise in the fault family today.)

dischargeSite.killRule: src/Precept/Pipeline/ProofEngine.Strategies.cs:678 -- if obligation.ReassignedBefore.Contains(fieldName) return false (a write to the log-by field earlier in the same action chain kills the guard fact: the membership the guard established is about the old collection value)

familyRespellability.argument: The only licensed discharge for KeyPresence(RequireAbsence:true) is the class-(c) guard `when not (F contains P)`. The sound-but-unprovable band is any program whose keys are genuinely unique by construction (e.g. a monotone fresh-key generator, or a first append onto a provably-empty log) but that carries no such guard. Every such program's business intent -- append a uniquely-keyed entry -- respells into the explicit guard, which passes at runtime exactly when the key is in fact fresh. The cost is authoring friction only, which the want doc deliberately embraces (want :137, 'forces authors to be more explicit'). No band member is inexpressible.
familyRespellability.bandMemberExample: A first `append ComplianceLog Note by Stamp` onto a default-empty log-by with no prior grow site is sound (empty collection contains no key) yet rejected today (verified: clean single-row unguarded append is Unresolved/PRE0101). Respelling: add `when not (ComplianceLog contains Stamp)`.
familyRespellability.corpusMeasurementStatus: pending (ratification layer 4). No log-by append-by uniqueness obligation appears discharged in samples/ today; the corpus cannot be cited as coverage.

cells.hostConstruct: transition row (from S on E ... -> append F V by K)
cells.obligationSchema: P not-in F -- the append-by ordering key P (the `by` operand) must not already be a key of the log-by field F, evaluated as the append action's own catalog-stamped precondition (RequireAbsence:true). Operand-free: the obligation is not an authored expression; P and F are recovered from the action's `by` slot and receiver.

routeSet.transportCite: transport-rule-restatement-2026-07-21 § 3, row `operand-free-action-precondition`: reached by 'fire (this row), inspect-fire, construction and its mirror'. Per the site-identity ruling (matrix § The minting rule, 'an evaluation site is an evaluation occasion, not a syntactic position'), the append mints one obligation per fire occasion selecting this row, each proved from that route's fired-guard fact.
reachedBy: fire selecting this transition row (guard evaluated at phase 2, action at phase 5)
construction + mirror only if this row is a construction row (does not arise here: construction rows cannot carry `transition` and append onto an initially-empty log; see openFlags)

premiseClassA_fieldModifiers.iff: never -- no field modifier on a log-by field expresses that a specific dynamic key value is absent from the collection. Class (a) instantiates nothing here.

premiseClassB_argConstraints.iff: never -- an argument constraint bounds the VALUE of the key P (its range/sign/length), never its MEMBERSHIP in F. No arg-constraint interval implies `P not-in F`.

premiseClassC_handlerGuard.iff: The obligation discharges IFF the transition row's `when` guard contains a conjunct normal-form-equal to `not (F contains P)` -- i.e. a `not` over a `contains` whose left operand is the log-by field F -- AND (transport frame) F is not written by any construct on the route between the guard's evaluation (phase 2) and the append site (phase 5): F not in mayWrite(guard, site). In the shipped analyzer the frame check is F not in obligation.ReassignedBefore (ProofEngine.Strategies.cs:678).
premiseClassC_handlerGuard.decisionProcedure: Finite walk of the guard's AND-conjuncts (ExtractGuardBranches + WalkForContains, ProofEngine.Strategies.cs:689/1295) for a `not (F contains .)` node whose contains-left field name equals F's. Reject (leave Unresolved, emit PRE0101) if no such conjunct exists, or if F was reassigned earlier in this action chain. The guard set is finite (statically declared), so non-existence is decidable. Strategy: GuardInPath.
premiseClassC_handlerGuard.searchBound: one pass over the guard conjunct tree; no fixpoint (expressions are finite loop-free trees, spec §0.4).

premiseClassD_preStateInductive.iff: not applicable in general -- no constraint shape in the language expresses 'this incoming key is absent from this append-only log' as an invariant over reachable configurations, and there is no establishment/preservation machinery for collection-membership facts (ProofRequirement carries no such subtype), so the citation duty (matrix § The cell, 2026-07-21 ruling) could not be satisfied even if a fact were available. One sound sub-case -- F provably empty on the route -- is NOT licensed today and sits in the respellability band (see openFlags: empty-collection-subcase).

citationDuty.factConsumed: a fired-guard fact (class c): the guard `not (F contains P)` evaluated true when this row was selected.
citationDuty.establishingObligation: the guard's own truth at fire time -- the row's actions run only if its guard evaluated true (spec:1897, 'guards select'), earned at phase 2 (transport-rule § 5, 'Fired-guard fact, earned at phase 2, immediately after that guard evaluates').
preservingObligations: the transport frame condition: no construct on the route between phase-2 guard evaluation and the phase-5 append writes F (F not in mayWrite(guard, site)); shipped as the ReassignedBefore kill at ProofEngine.Strategies.cs:678.
citationDuty.note: The class-(c) guard fact is route-local -- established and consumed within a single operation -- so it carries no construction-establishment / every-write-preservation chain of the kind a declared field modifier or invariant would (matrix § validity argument 'Guard normal-form match'). The citation is therefore the fired-guard provenance plus the frame, not a whole-file establish+preserve set.

openFlags: occasion-axis-incoherence: the coordinate map labels this cell's occasion 'operand-free-action-precondition' (an evaluation-site-category from the transport-rule axis) while the sibling cells use 'state-hook-action-operand' / 'stateless-hook-action-operand' (operand categories). But the KeyPresence obligation is operand-free (a catalog-stamped action precondition, no authored expression) in ALL THREE cells, so under the transport rule's own axis all three are 'operand-free-action-precondition' and the host construct (transition / state-hook / stateless-hook) is a separate coordinate. The map mixes host-construct into the evaluation-site-category axis. Transport-rule § 3 itself routes this: 'The occasion unit is therefore an evaluation event at a catalog-stamped fault site, not an occurrence of a written expression ... routed in § Open questions, because the matrix reserves the minting rule.' Not derivable from the matrix's generative sections -> owner ruling owed on how operand-free preconditions are keyed across host constructs.

construction-route-open: transport-rule § 3 marks operand-free-action-precondition as reached by 'construction and its mirror', but construction rows cannot carry `transition` (spec:1932) and land on an initially-empty log, and 'whether entry actions fire at construction' is unruled (spec §3A.4 Still unsettled). Whether a construction-route append-by mints/discharges is open.

state-action-construction-route-open: transport-rule § 3 routes 'construction if the anchor is the initial state', and spec §3A.4 leaves 'whether entry actions fire at construction and on a self-transition' unsettled. If S is the initial state, whether the `to S` entry-action append-by mints on the construction route (and whether a construction-route append onto the initially-empty log is trivially discharged) is open.

multi-state-action-ordering-not-must-run: if S carries more than one state action, spec §3A.4 leaves their multiplicity and order unsettled, so no state action on S is 'must-run' (transport-rule § 5 kill-on-may/establish-on-must). A guard fact earned in one such action does not establish for a sibling action's append site. The single-action witness here sidesteps this; a multi-action shape would need the guard on the appending action itself.

premiseClassC_handlerGuard.iffAndConflict: Discharges IFF the stateless hook's `when` guard contains a conjunct normal-form-equal to `not (F contains P)` on F, with the same transport frame. THIS DEPENDS ON A GUARD BEING ADMISSIBLE ON A STATELESS HOOK -- which is a spec-vs-implementation conflict (see openFlags: stateless-handler-guard-spec-conflict). The matrix's own generative content treats a stateless `on E when <guard>` as a class-(c) discharge (Witness Family 1 Base A, marked live-verified ✓v), and the shipped implementation parses and uses the guard (EventHandlerContext h => h.Handler.Guard, ProofEngine.Strategies.cs:684). This cell is authored on that basis. IF spec:1007 ('Handlers do not support when guards') is enforced instead, class (c) becomes structurally unavailable and -- since (a),(b),(d) are all inapplicable -- the obligation would have NO licensed discharge in a bare stateless hook, making append-by uniqueness undischargeable there.

premiseClassC_handlerGuard.searchBound: one pass over the guard conjunct tree.

stateless-handler-guard-spec-conflict: THE LOAD-BEARING FLAG for this cell. spec/precept-language-spec.md:1007 (§ Stateless event hook) states verbatim 'Handlers do not support when guards or a trailing ensure'. But (1) the shipped implementation parses and uses a stateless-hook guard -- verified: `on RecordEvent when not (ComplianceLog contains RecordEvent.Timestamp) -> append ...` compiles clean with KeyPresence Proved GuardInPath; (2) samples/Test2.precept:4 ('on Add1 when Add1.Amount1 + Add1.Amount2 <= 1000') uses one; (3) the matrix's Witness Family 1 Base A treats a stateless `on Add when <guard>` as a class-(c) discharge marked ✓v. The three disagree with spec:1007. This determines whether cell 3 has ANY licensed discharge: class (c) is the sole applicable premise class, and it exists only if the guard is admissible. Routed to owner (a spec-vs-implementation-vs-matrix conflict, not resolvable in this cell). Cross-check git history before ruling (deleted-doc precedent).

empty-collection-subcase: a first `append F V by K` in a stateless hook onto a default-empty log-by is sound (empty log has no key) but rejected today. Whether to license an emptiness-establishment discharge (analogous to the collection-growth `count>0` establishment at ProofEngine.Strategies.cs:706) is unrouted. Band member, respellable:yes (add the guard).

familyOpenFlags: key-argument-not-matched-hole (SOUNDNESS-CORRECTION CANDIDATE, not among the two listed known holes): the discharge walk WalkForContains (src/Precept/Pipeline/ProofEngine.Strategies.cs:1295-1332) matches only the contains-LEFT field name (fr.FieldName == fieldName), never the contained KEY operand. So `when not (F contains OtherKey)` discharges an `append F V by ActualKey` even when OtherKey != ActualKey. Verified @ HEAD: `when not (ComplianceLog contains RecordWrongKey.OtherTimestamp)` while appending `by RecordWrongKey.Timestamp` -> success:true, KeyPresence Proved GuardInPath, and an append with a colliding Timestamp is admitted. The matrix definition requires the guard conjunct to be normal-form-equal to `ActualKey not-in F` (the SPECIFIC append key), so the definition REJECTS this while the shipped compiler ACCEPTS it. Consequence for this family: all near-misses above use wrong-POLARITY (which the compiler correctly rejects), never wrong-KEY (which it wrongly accepts); a wrong-key near-miss could not be used as a rejecting oracle row. Route to /design as a soundness-correction with the witness program (major definition version, breaks certificate replay for KeyPresence cells).

operand-free-precondition-minting-phrasing-gap: the site-identity ruling (matrix § The minting rule) is phrased over 'one written expression reached by several routes'. The KeyPresence precondition is operand-free (no written expression), so the ruling's phrasing does not literally reach it. transport-rule § 3 already records this ('The occasion unit is therefore an evaluation event at a catalog-stamped fault site, not an occurrence of a written expression ... routed'). Recorded here as the minting-rule phrasing gap that governs the whole family's occasion count; owner ruling owed, per the matrix's reservation that the minting rule is 'never adjusted in passing'.
